meta.title: Next Session — Candidate Scenes
meta.subtitle: The GM's working slate for the 22nd (into Fall 1224), built on three spines: Wilhelm's delivery run to Scarem Montem, Dagmar's push into the regiones gated behind Tormente, and Confluensis turning the screws on the home front. Forward-looking only — beats played in the 2026-08-08 session have moved to the Chronicle and the Open Questions. Derived from the Open Questions prep hub (q027, t078).

meta.status_note: Developed = prepped and ready to stage · Deferred = deliberately left to improvise · Needs prep = flagged but not yet developed

scenes.title: What Wilhelm's assistants bring back — and can it break the thesis?
scenes.hook: Wilhelm's research assistants return from the winter gathering (sent west and south, paid in grain and silver). The live beat is whether any of it FALSIFIES the folk-magic thesis rather than confirming it.
scenes.detail: ADVANCED (Summer 1224): Carl & Isaac returned — the technique worked but the madness cost was realized (a suicide and a double killing among ~12-15 students); the temporal mage's brass ACORN turned up with no magic residue. The weak maritime citation is still unfilled, and still gates the delivery (s6). A negative result — a tradition that works without leaning on the environment, or the missing open-ocean storm-prediction / current-finding citation turning out not to exist — forces Wilhelm to revise before he can deliver to Scarem Montem (see s6). Developed: the negation is a MADNESS failure rate that breaks the scalable / vis-factory case without disproving the magic itself; the assistants also flag a temporal hedge mage who beat the Limit of Time, leaving Wilhelm an origin-less brass acorn.

scenes.title: Éogan and the capricorn
scenes.hook: On the voyage home from Ireland a Magic-realm capricorn (sea-goat) singles Éogan out and paces his ship — offered as his first familiar prospect. The work is courting it and the binding lab-work, not an instant bond.
scenes.detail: ADVANCED (Spring 1224): Éogan spotted the capricorn at a river-mouth near Drogheda (it favours salt-meets-fresh water), took a water sample and cast a relocation spell. Courtship and binding are still ahead. Developed: the draw is independent of the 'small fae drawn to Éogan/Stijntje' affinity; its signature specialty is CROSSING THRESHOLDS INTO REGIONES (mythic grounding in Enki's Goat-Fish and Macrobius's Gate of the Gods). Corpus build/bind references and a suggested Might ~12–16 Magic build are recorded. What it wants in exchange remains open.

scenes.title: Does Wilhelm sail to Scarem Montem? — and the three sealed chests
scenes.hook: The ship-for-book swap is in motion — the Hound of Cassel is under Wilhelm's control and headed back to Scarem Montem, and what he owes them is the folk-magic thesis. Whether he arrives with a finished thesis or one still short its maritime example hinges on s1.
scenes.detail: SET UP (Summer 1224): Wilhelm now has the Hound of Cassel and found the three sealed chests aboard (held from the Scarem Montem raid; still unopened, boat warded). The delivery is next session's anchor. Developed: the three sealed chests aboard the Hound of Cassel are intercepted Bishopric-of-Liège ↔ Scarem Montem cipher letters exposing a Church/State suborning — a Code violation tied to the Brabant conspiracy. Ring-based public/private-key crypto lets the covenant PROVE the correspondents but mostly not read the content. Wilhelm may be carrying Scarem Montem's own incriminating mail back to them: return it, keep it, or weaponise it in the swap? The Hound itself is warded with a 1-month-duration ward against scrying, cast by Wilhelm, for the run to Scarem Montem.

scenes.title: Return to Tormente — with Mímormr's token
scenes.thread: The dragon errand / the Carnac regio
scenes.hook: Dagmar carries Mímormr's token back to Tormente, expecting passage into the Carnac regio — but Tormente sent him to free a prisoner it had bound, and may not deal straight.
scenes.detail: Tormente framed itself as 'estranged kin' and used Dagmar to break Mímormr's binding. What Tormente actually wanted, whether it honours the regio bargain, and how it reacts to Mímormr's freedom (and the stolen five bags of gold, if noticed) are all live. Flagged for the 22nd as the return to the first dragon.

scenes.title: Into the magical regio — and Llewellyn's gambit
scenes.hook: Once Tormente grants passage, the party enters the Aquam-tinged Carnac regio — where Llewellyn hopes the irregular time-flow will let him safely unwind his Zeno's-paradox longevity working.
scenes.detail: Llewellyn wants to 'catch the tide going out' — end his half-life-forever working in a place where time runs irregular, ideally with backup, before a sudden failure turns catastrophic. His found time-quartz crystal reads the flows. What the regio holds, and whether the gambit works, is the payoff.

scenes.title: The regiones behind Tormente
scenes.thread: The dragon errand / the Carnac regio
scenes.hook: The next-session objective for the northern party: reach the regiones gated behind Tormente — more than one lies back there.
scenes.detail: Umbrella objective for the 22nd. Beyond Tormente's ground sits a cluster of regiones — the Aquam-tinged Carnac regio (s9) and whatever else the dragon conceals. Runs straight off s8 (the return with Mímormr's token) and into s9 (Llewellyn's time-flow gambit inside the regio).

scenes.title: Confluensis turns the screws — the Grand Tribunal complaint
scenes.hook: The home-front spine for the 22nd: after the public 13th-place "Siege of Shame" at the 1223 Tribunal and Bertrand's cold renege of the book-storage deal, Confluensis moves from soured silence to active reprisal — assembling a complaint against Sjórseiðr while the covenant's magi are scattered north (Dagmar/Valdemar) and south (Wilhelm).
scenes.detail: The documented direction (c022): someone from Confluensis is preparing to bring Rán's open faerie association — and the covenant's OTHER exposed edges — before the Grand Tribunal as a bundled quaesitorial complaint. Live edges it could gather: Valdemar parading the sea-fae Rán at the feast (c022), the unspendable five bags of stolen Roman dragon-gold and its provenance (c026), Mímormr loosed toward the North Sea by Dagmar's errand (t072), and — most dangerous — Wilhelm's ungifted folk-magic teaching with its madness/death toll (t019, t020, q028). Oleron, a Liege that favours Sjórseiðr for beating the other lieges, is the natural counter-ally (t074). What FORM the screw-turning takes first — a formal charge, a whispering campaign, vassal-poaching, or economic pressure through the soured Bertrand arrangement — is the live beat. GM prep 2026-08-09 (t078).

scenes.title: Harvesting the Diedne Garden — what does it entail?
scenes.hook: Valdemar has taken on the covenant's newly-won Diedne Garden — a Herbam vis source (3 pawns/yr). What tending and harvesting it actually entails is undeveloped: the harvest mechanics, any guardian or condition, and — given the name — whether a vanished Diedne magus left something in it no one has yet seen.
scenes.detail: Flagged from Valdemar's declared season plans (t079) and the 2026-08-08 recap, where he 'defaulted to taking care of the Diedne Garden' and said he wanted to keep an eye on it — wondering whether its Diedne maker left a remnant behind. TO PREP: how the Herbam vis is harvested (the season/window, the roll, any risk of botch or aura harm); the garden's nature and location; whether there is a guardian, ward, or standing condition on the harvest; and what — if anything — a long-dead Diedne planter concealed there. Pointed resonance: Valdemar is himself secretly House Diedne (t078), so a Diedne garden is a personal draw as much as a practical one. He also means to pick up the basics of Herbam in order to work it.

scenes.title: Raising Nóatún — the covenant's Isle-of-Man manor, hall, and Valdemar's laboratory
scenes.hook: Valdemar builds out the covenant's Isle-of-Man harbour holding — Ránargarðr (“Rán's Garden”) — raising the main hall Nóatún, where the coven Winters, and his own Undrahöll (“Hall of Wonders”), whose ratified laboratory he means to work through the cold months, funded by the summer and fall raiding and trading.
scenes.detail: The lab is speced and ratified (full player notes + rulings live in t079's dossier): a modified Viking longhouse — Size 13 / Refinement 0 / Safety 0 / General Quality +1 / Aesthetics +11 — 60£ to raise (Superior Construction doubling the bill), Upkeep 4 (~5£/yr at Valdemar's Winter-only use), with living quarters for him and Rán kept separate from the lab for Safety. The Diedne Garden (see s12) sits within the same Ránargarðr holding. TO RESOLVE IN PLAY: the raiding/trading that funds the 60£ build and its upkeep; Valdemar's final laboratory specialization picks (runes vs Techniques/Forms, per the ruling that viktir work as spells); and which season(s) the construction consumes. Once this beat is played, its outcomes merge back into the t079 dossier.
